title: Dual Spaces Adjoint Operators and Annihilators

items.title: The continuous dual, its completeness, and evaluation
items.statement: Recall X*=B(X,K), a Banach space even when X is incomplete, and <f,x>=f(x). This is a bilinear pairing, not an inner product.

references.title: Bühler–Salamon, Functional Analysis, §§1.3.1–1.3.2, Theorem 1.31 and (1.22), pp.31–32

items.title: Annihilator notation and the preannihilator
items.statement: For M subset X, M-perp={f in X*: f|M=0}, agreeing with the published subspace definition after taking span M. For N subset X*, preannihilator N={x in X: f(x)=0 for every f in N}.

references.title: Brezis, Functional Analysis, Sobolev Spaces and PDEs, §1.3, notation p.9

items.title: Annihilators and preannihilators are norm closed
items.statement: Both annihilators in X* and preannihilators in X are norm-closed linear subspaces, for arbitrary subsets M,N.

references.title: Brezis, Functional Analysis, Sobolev Spaces and PDEs, §1.3, notation before Proposition 1.9, p.9

items.proof_strategy: Intersect kernels of evaluation maps; |f(x)|<=||f||||x|| gives continuity in either variable.

items.title: The dual of a quotient is its annihilator
items.statement: For normed X and closed M, q-pullback maps (X/M)* onto M-perp as a linear isometry.
items.proof_strategy: Factor a functional vanishing on M through cosets; prove representative independence before applying the quotient universal property and its norm equality. No HB needed in this direction.

items.title: The dual of a closed subspace is a dual quotient
items.statement: For closed M in normed X, restriction induces an onto linear isometry X*/M-perp -> M*. Restriction is contractive, norm one if M is nonzero and zero if M=0.
items.proof_strategy: Restrictions of representatives agree; kernel is M-perp. HB supplies a norm-preserving extension, minimizing norm in each coset. Thus surjectivity and isometry are separate verified claims.

items.title: Distance to an annihilator is the restriction norm
items.statement: For closed M in X and f in X*, dist(f,M-perp)=||f|M||.
items.proof_strategy: Unpack the quotient norm in the restriction isometry.

items.title: The transpose of a bounded operator
items.statement: For bounded K-linear T:X->Y define T*:Y*->X* by T*g=g composed with T; this is the Banach adjoint, distinguished from the future Hilbert adjoint.

items.title: The transpose is bounded with the same norm
items.statement: T* is bounded K-linear and ||T*||=||T|| for normed X,Y.
items.proof_strategy: The composition estimate gives <=. Norm each nonzero Tx with a unit functional for the reverse inequality, including zero operators separately.

items.title: Transposition reverses composition
items.statement: For T:X->Y and S:Y->Z, (ST)*=T*S*; identity transposes to identity. Transposition is K-linear on operators.
items.proof_strategy: Evaluate every map on g and x; associativity and scalar linearity give the identities.

items.title: Elementary kernel and range annihilator identities
items.statement: For bounded T:X->Y between normed spaces: (ran T)-perp=ker T*, preannihilator(ran T*)=ker T, and closure(ran T)=preannihilator(ker T*), with norm closure in Y.

references.title: Bühler–Salamon, Functional Analysis, Theorem 4.8(i), pp.174; Corollary 2.55, p.84

items.proof_strategy: The first identity is composition; for the second norming separates Tx from zero. Apply the published primal annihilator-closure theorem for the third. This independent lemma carries all norm-topology uses; no FA-8 result is invoked.

items.title: Dense range is equivalent to injectivity of the transpose
items.statement: For bounded T between normed spaces, closure(ran T)=Y iff ker T*={0}.
items.proof_strategy: Use the third elementary identity and the zero annihilator criterion.

items.title: The canonical evaluation map into the bidual
items.statement: For normed X, define J_X:X->X** by (J_X x)(f)=f(x). Boundedness of each evaluation follows from the dual-norm inequality.

items.title: The canonical bidual map is an isometry
items.statement: J_X is K-linear and ||J_X x||=||x|| for every x in any normed space X.
items.proof_strategy: Use |f(x)|<=||f||||x|| and a norming functional for x nonzero; handle x=0 separately.

items.title: Distance to a closed subspace via unit annihilators
items.statement: For closed M in normed X, dist(x,M)=sup{|f(x)|: f in M-perp, ||f||<=1}.
items.proof_strategy: Apply bidual norm equality in X/M and identify its dual by Q. The unit-ball supremum covers M=X without an empty supremum convention.

items.title: The canonical map is natural
items.statement: For bounded T:X->Y, T** J_X=J_Y T.
items.proof_strategy: Evaluate both sides on arbitrary g in Y*.

items.title: Reflexivity is surjectivity of the canonical map
items.statement: A Banach space X is reflexive when J_X is onto. An unspecified isomorphism X ~= X** does not define reflexivity.

items.title: Membership in the transpose range by an operator estimate
items.statement: For bounded T:X->Y and f in X*, f=T*g for some g in Y* iff |f(x)|<=C||Tx|| for all x and some C>=0. In the latter case one can choose ||g||<=C.
items.proof_strategy: Define h(Tx)=f(x); the bound proves independence of x and boundedness on ran T, even if that range is not closed. HB extends h to Y.

items.title: Closed range is equivalent to a quotient estimate
items.statement: Assume DC. For bounded T between Banach spaces, ran T is closed iff dist(x,ker T)<=C||Tx|| for all x and some C>0.
items.proof_strategy: The induced map X/ker T -> ran T is bounded and bijective; if the range is closed use bounded inverse. Conversely its map into Y is bounded below from a Banach domain, giving closed range. The kernel is closed by continuity.

items.title: A lower bound for the transpose forces a dense image of a ball
items.statement: If ||g||<=C||T*g|| for all g in Y*, C>0, then B_Y(0,1/C) is contained in the norm closure of T(B_X(0,1)). X,Y need only be normed.

references.title: Bühler–Salamon, Functional Analysis, Theorem 4.16 proof (vii) => (i), (4.10)–(4.11), p.180

items.proof_strategy: Separate a point outside the closed convex balanced image-ball closure. Its support supremum is ||T*g||; use real parts over C and phase rotation. A point of norm <1/C contradicts ||g||<=C||T*g||. This lemma does not use closed-range equivalence.

items.title: Surjectivity is equivalent to a lower bound for the transpose
items.statement: Assume DC. For bounded T:X->Y between Banach spaces, T is onto iff some C>0 satisfies ||g||<=C||T*g|| for all g in Y*.

references.title: Bühler–Salamon, Functional Analysis, Corollary 4.17(i), p.181, with Theorem 4.16 p.180

items.proof_strategy: Forward: the quantitative open-mapping ball inclusion gives the lower bound by taking suprema. Reverse: BALL plus the published successive approximation lemma gives an actual ball of radius 1/(2C) in T(B_X), hence onto. Do not derive this reverse direction from the closed-range theorem being proved next.

items.title: Banach closed-range theorem
items.statement: Assume DC. For bounded T:X->Y between Banach spaces the ranges of T and T* are norm closed simultaneously; each is equivalent to dist(x,ker T)<=C||Tx||. When closed, ran T=preannihilator(ker T*) and ran T*=(ker T)-perp.
items.proof_strategy: Forward: EST bounds every f annihilating ker T by C||f||||Tx||; FAC yields the exact transpose range, which is norm closed. Reverse: apply EST to T* (both duals Banach), set Y0=closure ran T and S:T:X->Y0. Restriction Y*->Y0* is onto with kernel ker T*. Its quotient norm is the distance to ker T*, so the estimate on T* gives ||h||<=C||S*h||. SUR makes S onto Y0. Finish primal identity with E. No reflexivity or weak-star closure is assumed.

items.title: Bounded below is equivalent to surjectivity of the transpose
items.statement: Assume DC. For bounded T between Banach spaces, T is bounded below iff T* is onto.
items.proof_strategy: Bounded below gives injective closed range, so the closed-range identity makes T* onto. Conversely onto implies ker T=0 by E and ran T closed by CR; apply the published bounded-below criterion.

items.title: Invertibility and the inverse of the transpose
items.statement: Assume DC. T between Banach spaces is bijective iff T* is bijective, and then (T*)^{-1}=(T^{-1})*. A surjective isometry T has a surjective isometry T*, and conversely.
items.proof_strategy: Combine injectivity/surjectivity criteria. Transpose the two inverse identities; compare the operator and inverse norms. BS uses isometry here to mean a bijective isometry, as its proof explicitly assumes. Never extend this to arbitrary isometric embeddings.

items.title: Finite truncations approximate null and summable sequences
items.statement: For K=R or C and P_N retaining coordinates 0,...,N, ||x-P_N x||_infinity ->0 for x in c0 and ||a-P_N a||_1 ->0 for a in ell-one. Here ell-one(K) consists of sequences with sum |a_n|<infinity.
items.proof_strategy: The errors are respectively sup_{n>N}|x_n| and sum_{n>N}|a_n|. Define the complex sequence model explicitly, with coordinatewise operations and the absolute-sum norm; scalar series convergence justifies the norm and pairing.

items.title: The continuous dual of c0 is ell-one
items.statement: Over K=R or C, a maps to [x -> sum_{n>=0} a_n x_n] is a linear isometric bijection ell-one(K)->c0(K)*.
items.proof_strategy: For f define a_n=f(e_n). For each finite prefix use x_n=conj(a_n)/|a_n| when nonzero, else 0, to bound its absolute sum by ||f||. Absolute convergence yields a functional; finite-truncation density recovers f. The same finite test vectors prove norm equality. No conjugate is inserted into the pairing.

items.title: The complex continuous dual of ell-one is ell-infinity
items.statement: For complex sequence spaces, b -> [a -> sum b_n a_n] is a linear isometric bijection ell-infinity(C)->ell-one(C)*. The real counterpart is the already-published counting-measure corollary.

references.title: Bühler–Salamon, Functional Analysis, Example 1.35, p.36 (scalar-field extension of its coefficient proof)

items.proof_strategy: For f, coefficients b_n=f(e_n) are bounded by ||f||. Absolute convergence defines the pairing and truncation proves representation. Testing e_n yields the supremum lower bound, with no requirement that a maximum exists.

items.title: The published Lp duality theorem in abstract notation
items.statement: For the real spaces and sigma-finite measure in the published theorem, 1<=p<infinity and conjugate q give a linear isometric identification (Lp)* ~= Lq. In particular the real ell-one dual is ell-infinity. No p=infinity surjectivity, complex extension, or arbitrary-measure generalization is claimed.

references.title: Bühler–Salamon, Functional Analysis, Example 1.33, p.33 and Example 1.35, p.36

items.title: The weak-star topology from finite evaluations
items.statement: For a real or complex normed space X, sigma(X*,X) is the initial topology of the evaluations f -> f(x), x in X, into K with its usual topology. At f0 a neighbourhood basis consists of {f: |(f-f0)(x_j)|<epsilon for 1<=j<=n}, with finitely many x_j in X and epsilon>0; n=0 gives X*. Weak-star closure means topological closure in this topology, not sequential closure.

references.title: Bühler–Salamon, Functional Analysis, Example 3.9(i), p.122; Lemma 3.6(i), pp.119–120 (real source; complex disk version via the same initial-topology construction)

items.title: Finite evaluations separate a functional from a dual subspace
items.statement: Let N be a K-linear subspace of X*, let x_1,...,x_n in X, n>=1, and let E(f)=(f(x_1),...,f(x_n)). If E(f0) is not in E(N), there exists x in span{x_1,...,x_n} with g(x)=0 for every g in N and f0(x)=1. No completeness of X or closedness of N is assumed.

references.title: Bühler–Salamon, Functional Analysis, Theorem 3.12(ii), pp.125–127, and Corollary 3.26(i), p.130; finite-coordinate adaptation using Theorem 2.53, pp.82–83

items.proof_strategy: E(N) is a linear subspace of K^n, hence finite dimensional and closed. Apply geometric Hahn–Banach in K^n to E(N) and E(f0), obtaining a K-linear h with h|E(N)=0 and h(E(f0))=1. Put a_j=h(e_j) and x=sum_j a_j x_j. Expansion in the standard coordinate basis gives h(E(f))=sum_j a_j f(x_j)=f(x); no complex conjugates occur. This is a finite-dimensional implementation of the source separation step, not an appeal to unplanned locally convex separation.

items.title: Double annihilators give norm and weak-star closures
items.statement: For a K-linear subspace N of X*, (preannihilator N)-perp equals the sigma(X*,X) closure of N. Thus N is weak-star closed iff it equals its double annihilator, and weak-star dense iff its preannihilator is zero. The primal identity preannihilator(M-perp)=norm closure(M), for a linear subspace M of X, is recalled from cor-annihilator-detects-closure rather than proved a second time. X need only be normed.

references.title: Bühler–Salamon, Functional Analysis, Corollary 3.26(i)–(iii), p.130; Corollary 2.55, p.84 (real source; K-linear finite-coordinate proof covers C)

items.proof_strategy: Every evaluation at x in preannihilator N vanishes on N and has a closed kernel in sigma(X*,X), proving closure(N) is contained in its double annihilator. Conversely, if f0 is outside closure(N), choose a basic finite-evaluation neighbourhood disjoint from N. It has n>=1 since N contains zero. Its coordinate map E satisfies E(f0) not in E(N). The preceding separation lemma gives x in preannihilator N with f0(x)=1, excluding f0 from the double annihilator. Closedness is immediate; density uses that X* separates each nonzero x, already contained in the published primal annihilator-closure result with M={0}. Reuse that published result for the primal identity. No sequence characterization or Banach hypothesis is used.

items.title: Kernel-range identities and the weak-star closure of the transpose range
items.statement: For bounded T:X->Y between normed spaces, (ran T)-perp=ker T* and (ker T)-perp=weak-star closure(ran T*) in sigma(X*,X). Norm closure is not substituted.

references.title: Bühler–Salamon, Functional Analysis, Theorem 4.8 and Corollary 3.26, pp.174 and 130

items.proof_strategy: Apply the now preceding local bipolar-closure theorem to the linear subspace N=ran T*. The elementary preannihilator identity gives preannihilator(ran T*)=ker T. The first identity is the preceding elementary kernel-range lemma. Its injectivity consequence is that T is injective iff ran T* is weak-star dense. Preserve weak-star closure throughout.

title: Dual Spaces Adjoint Operators and Annihilators — Examples

items.title: Coordinate functionals on sequence spaces
items.statement: For each n>=0, x -> x_n has norm one on c0 and ell-one over R or C, represented by e_n in their identified duals.
items.proof_strategy: The coordinate bound gives <=1, and e_n attains one.

items.title: Transposes of the right and left shifts
items.statement: On c0 define R(x)=(0,x_0,x_1,...) and L(x)=(x_1,x_2,...). On the ell-one dual, R*=L and L*=R. The same formulas hold for ell-one and its ell-infinity dual.

references.title: Bühler–Salamon, Functional Analysis, Definition 4.1 and Examples 1.35–1.36, pp.172,36–37

items.proof_strategy: Check each shift preserves the stated sequence space and is bounded; reindex the absolutely convergent pairing. Define shifts explicitly, with indexing from zero.

items.title: Evaluation functionals and point masses
items.statement: For nonempty compact Hausdorff K and t in K, evaluation delta_t on C(K;C) has norm one and is represented by the regular point mass at t in RMK. For a homeomorphism phi, pullback sends delta_t under its transpose to delta_phi(t).

references.title: Bühler–Salamon, Functional Analysis, Example 1.37 and Example 4.4, pp.37,173

items.proof_strategy: The constant function one norms evaluation. Check Dirac regularity directly and integral f d delta_t=f(t), then invoke the published RMK uniqueness. Evaluate pullback at t.

items.title: The annihilator of a coordinate subspace
items.statement: For I subset N and M_I={x in c0:x_n=0 for n not in I}, its annihilator under c0*=ell-one is {a:a_n=0 for n in I}; the preannihilator of this last space is M_I.

references.title: Bühler–Salamon, Functional Analysis, Example 1.36, pp.36–37; Brezis §1.3 notation p.9

items.proof_strategy: Use e_n tests in both directions and the absolutely convergent coordinate pairing; M_I is an intersection of closed coordinate kernels.

items.title: Finite-dimensional duals and matrix transposes
items.statement: For a fixed basis of a finite-dimensional normed K-space, continuous and algebraic duals agree. Under dual-basis coordinates, a matrix A has Banach transpose A^t over R or C, without conjugation.
items.proof_strategy: Coordinate estimates give boundedness of all linear functionals using norm equivalence; expand sum_i g_i sum_j A_ij x_j. This is not the Hilbert conjugate transpose.

items.title: The dual construction reverses arrows
items.statement: The claim that T:X->Y canonically induces by composition an arrow X*->Y* is false. For inclusion i:K->K^2, i*=coordinate restriction (K^2)*->K*.

references.title: Bühler–Salamon, Functional Analysis, Definition 4.1 and Lemma 4.3(i), pp.172–173

items.proof_strategy: Write i(t)=(t,0); composition of g(s,t)=as+bt with i is at. The proposed same-direction composition is not defined for a functional on K. No claim that all conceivable covariant assignments are impossible.

items.title: The canonical bidual map of c0 misses the constant sequence
items.statement: Under the dual identifications, J_c0 is the inclusion c0 -> ell-infinity; the bounded sequence (1,1,...) is not in its image.

references.title: Bühler–Salamon, Functional Analysis, Examples 1.35–1.36 and §2.4.1, pp.36–37,88

items.proof_strategy: Evaluate J_x on the coefficient functional associated with a in ell-one; it is sum a_n x_n. Every possible preimage of (1,1,...) would have all coordinates one and hence would not lie in c0.

items.title: The transpose of an injective map need not have norm-dense range
items.statement: Over R, inclusion T:ell-one->c0 is injective and has dense range. Its transpose is ell-one->ell-infinity, whose norm closure is c0, a proper subspace of (ker T)-perp=ell-infinity.
items.proof_strategy: Compute T* by the pairing. Finite support sequences imply norm closure contains c0; ell-one is contained in the closed c0 subspace, proving equality. The constant-one sequence is outside. No weak-star result is needed for this norm-closure refutation.

items.title: Injective transpose does not imply surjectivity
items.statement: On real ell-two let (Tx)_n=x_n/(n+1). T and its transpose under counting-measure duality are injective with dense, nonclosed range, but neither is onto.

references.title: Bühler–Salamon, Functional Analysis, Example 4.9, p.174; Brezis Remark 20, p.48

items.proof_strategy: Finite sequences belong to the range and approximate every ell-two vector by tails. The target y_n=1/(n+1) lies in ell-two, but its forced preimage (1,1,...) does not. Bound the sum of 1/(n+1)^2 by telescoping for n>=1. Compute the transpose by the real pairing.

items.title: Two different Riesz representation theorems
items.statement: RMK identifies the complex dual of C_0(K) with regular measures; the Hilbert-space Riesz theorem belongs to the later Hilbert geometry page. Evaluation is not an inner-product identification.

references.title: Bühler–Salamon, Functional Analysis, Examples 1.32 and 1.37, pp.32,37
